question.text: Vaidya Debt AIF (Category II) is valuing a INR 1,000 par bond held in portfolio. Coupon = 10% p.a. (annual), 4 years to maturity. Required yield (YTM) = 8%. Use PVA factor at 8%, 4 yrs = 3.312 and PV factor at 8%, 4 yrs = 0.735. Fair value of the bond?

explanation.text: The Logic: Bond fair value V = I x PVA(r, n) + F x PV(r, n), where I is the annual coupon, F is the face value, and r and n are the yield and maturity. Here: V = 100 x 3.312 + 1,000 x 0.735 = 331.20 + 735.00 = INR 1,066.20. Because YTM (8%) is below the coupon (10%), the bond trades at a premium to par. The Trap: INR 1,000.00 assumes par and ignores the differential between coupon and yield. INR 950.40 reflects a discount, which would arise if YTM were above the coupon. INR 1,100.00 miscounts the principal redemption. Note: The relationship between coupon and YTM determines whether the bond trades at par, premium, or discount.
